Rashi on Keritot 7a:10:1.hebrew: במבעט - ביוה"כ, דאמר: לא תכפר עליו. משום הכי לא תני ליה:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:10:1.english: To one who rejects - [Rejecting] Yom Kippur, as he says: "Let it not atone for him." That is why [the Tanna] did not teach it.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:12:1.english: And it is a logical inference - That it should not atone [for those who do not repent].

Rashi on Keritot 7a:12:2.english: Only for those who repent - For we require [it to be brought] of his own will.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:13:1.hebrew: אשם - לאו דוקא נקט, דהא אשכחן אשם אמזיד בפרק שני (לקמן כריתות ח:): ד' מביאין על הזדון:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:13:1.english: A guilt offering - [The Tanna] mentioned [this] not precisely, for behold, we find a guilt offering for an intentional [sin] in the second chapter (below, Keritot 8b): “Four bring [an offering] for an intentional [sin].”

Rashi on Keritot 7a:13:2.english: Yet - [As the verse states: “Yet] on the tenth of the month it is Yom Kippur.”

Rashi on Keritot 7a:13:3.hebrew: חלק - יום כפור לשבין, ולא לשאינן שבין:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:13:3.english: Divided - Yom Kippur [atones] for those who repent, and not for those who do not repent.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:14:1.english: What is [meant by] “those who repent” - Where [the baraita] teaches: “They atone only for those who repent.”

Rashi on Keritot 7a:14:2.hebrew: הא קתני לא אם אמרת כו' - וא"כ, מאי קאמר? היינו הך:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:14:2.english: Behold, it teaches: No, if you said, etc. - And if so, what is it saying? It is the very same thing.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:15:1.hebrew: אלא כי הא כו' - והיינו דקאמר: חטאת אינו מכפר אלא על השבין, ששבין משעת הפרשה עד שעת הקרבה, ולא שהמיר דתו בינתיים. והתם בעי למילף יוה"כ, דאם המיר דת קודם יוה"כ וחזר בו אחר יוה"כ, תו לא מכפר עליה יום הכפורים אחר על עבירותיו שמקמי המרתו:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:15:1.english: Rather, like that, etc. - And this is what it means when it says: A sin offering atones only for those who repent — who are penitent from the time of designation until the time of sacrifice, and not that he apostatized in the interim. And there, [the baraita] sought to derive regarding Yom Kippur that if he apostatized before Yom Kippur and retracted [his apostasy] after Yom Kippur, another Yom Kippur will no longer atone for him for his transgressions from before his apostasy.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:16:1.hebrew: אמאי נהי - דבקרבן אמרינן: הואיל ונדחה לאחר הפרשה — ידחה מעל המזבח, אבל גברא לגבי יוה"כ בר כפרה הוא, כישראל מעליא:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:16:1.english: Why? Granted - For regarding a sacrifice, we say that since it was rejected after designation, it shall be rejected from upon the altar; but the person, with regard to Yom Kippur, is fit for atonement, like a proper Israelite.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:17:1.hebrew: ורמינהו - אהא דתני לעיל: יוה"כ אינו מכפר אלא על השבין:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:17:1.english: And they raise a contradiction - Against that which was taught above: “Yom Kippur atones only for those who repent.”

Rashi on Keritot 7a:17:2.english: A holy convocation - By arranging the order of the prayer.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:18:1.hebrew: ה"ג: לא קשיא: הא — ר' יהודה, הא — רבי:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:18:1.english: This is the reading: “This is not difficult: this [baraita] is Rabbi Yehuda, [and] that [baraita] is Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi].”

Rashi on Keritot 7a:19:1.english: One who divests himself of the yoke - [The yoke] of all the commandments.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:19:2.hebrew: מגלה פנים - דורש באגדות של דופי, כגון מנשה שהיה אומר: מה היה לו למשה לומר, ״ותמנע היתה פילגש״:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:19:2.english: One who reveals facets - [One who] expounds homilies of reproach, such as Manasseh, who would say: What [need] was there for Moses to say, “And Timna was a concubine”?

Rashi on Keritot 7a:1:1.hebrew: שנשאת לישראל. ואינה משלמת חומש - דלא זרה, שהרי לא נתחללה — שאם ימות בעלה ותנשא לכהן, אוכלת; או אם זרע אין לה, הדרא לתרומה:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:1:1.english: [Who] married an Israelite. And she does not pay [the added] fifth - For she is not a stranger [to the priesthood], since she was not profaned — for if her husband dies and she marries a priest, she may eat [teruma], or if she has no offspring, she returns to [eating] teruma.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:1:2.english: She pays, etc. - We do not read [the word] “guilt offering.”

Rashi on Keritot 7a:20:1.hebrew: ברייתא דקתני יוה"כ מ"מ, רבי היא:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:20:1.english: The baraita that teaches [that] Yom Kippur [atones] in any case is [the opinion of] Rabbi.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:20:2.hebrew: מודה רבי בעבירות דיוה"כ - דהא דקתני: ״לא התענה בו מכפר״ — אעבירות דכל השנה, אבל ההיא עבירה דעינוי לא מכפר. ו״אך חלק״ נמי דקתני לעיל — בעבירות דיומיה קאמר:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:20:2.english: Rabbi concedes regarding the transgressions of Yom Kippur - For that which [the baraita] teaches, “[If] one did not afflict himself on it, [Yom Kippur] atones,” [means it atones] for the transgressions of the entire year; but for that transgression of [failing to observe the] affliction, it does not atone. And that which [the baraita] taught above as well, “'Yet' divided,” was speaking of the transgressions of the day itself.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:20:3.hebrew: יום הכפורים אינו מכפר אלא היום, כדכתיב (ויקרא ט״ז:ל׳) כי ביום הזה:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:20:3.english: Yom Kippur atones only during the day, as it is written: “For on this day” (Leviticus 16:30).

Rashi on Keritot 7a:20:4.hebrew: כרת - הולך ערירי בלא בנים, ואם יש לו — מתים:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:20:4.english: Karet - He goes childless, without children; and if he has [children], they die.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:22:1.english: Alternatively, where he performed labor close to sunset - As there was no time to effect atonement.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:22:2.hebrew: א"נ בהדי דעביד עבידתא פסקיה מרא דרפיק בה לשקיה ומית - מיד, דלא הוה שהות לכפורי:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:22:2.english: Alternatively, as he was performing labor, the hoe with which he was hoeing cut his leg and he died - [He died] immediately, as there was no time to effect atonement.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:23:1.english: This is the reading: “What [is meant by]: Even [one who] blasphemes?”

Rashi on Keritot 7a:24:1.hebrew: שמעו לר' עקיבא - דמתני' ר"ע היא, כדמפרש לקמן: ״מגדף מביא קרבן, דברי ר' עקיבא״; ואמרי: ״אף מגדף נמי כידעוני״. תימה לי: ולר' יוחנן, דאמר לעיל (כריתות דף ג:) ״הואיל ושניהם בלאו אחד נאמרו״ — מאי ״אף״ דקתני במתניתין:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:24:1.english: [The Rabbis] heard Rabbi Akiva - For our Mishnah is [the opinion of] Rabbi Akiva, as is explained below: “A blasphemer brings an offering, the words of Rabbi Akiva”; and they [the Rabbis] said: “Even a blasphemer too is like a sorcerer [yide'oni].” It is astonishing to me: according to Rabbi Yochanan, who said above (Keritot 3b), “Since both of them were stated in one prohibition,” what is [the meaning of] “even” that is taught in the Mishnah?

Rashi on Keritot 7a:25:1.english: And it says: “He shall bear his sin” - [The Gemara] explains below that the karet of a blasphemer deals with the offering for idol worship.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:2:1.hebrew: ומיתתה בחנק - ורבי מאיר לטעמיה, דאע"ג דמעיקרא לאו זרה היא, השתא מיהא זרה הויא:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:2:1.english: And her death is by strangulation - And Rabbi Meir [follows] his reasoning, that even though initially she was not a non-priest, now, in any case, she is a non-priest.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:3:1.english: And the Rabbis - This is Rabbi Yehuda, his disputant.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:3:2.english: Both this [case], etc. - For we require [that one be] a stranger from his beginning.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:4:1.english: And with the answers that we answered - That Rabbi Meir's reason is because it was equated with anointing.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:4:2.hebrew: אבל נתינה דעלמא - כגון לא יתן עליה לבונה דמנחת חוטא — בכזית, דילפינן מונתן לכהן את הקדש (ויקרא כ״ב:י״ד). והכי מפרשא בפרק כל המנחות באות מצה (מנחות נט:):
Rashi on Keritot 7a:4:2.english: But placing in general - For example, [the prohibition]: 'He shall not put frankincense upon it' [in the case of] the meal offering of a sinner [requires] an olive-bulk, as we derive from: 'And he shall give the holy thing to the priest' (Leviticus 22:14). And so it is explained in the chapter [entitled] 'Kol HaMenachot Ba'ot Matzah' (Menachot 59b).

Rashi on Keritot 7a:5:1.hebrew: לא ייסך כתיב - בשני יודין. שדי חדא לתוך התיבה וקרי ״לא יסיך״, דמשמע: מי שמצווה שלא יסיך — לא לעצמו ולא לאחרים — מצווה אחר עליו שלא לסוכו. ועובד כוכבים לאו בר מצוה הוא:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:5:1.english: “It shall not be applied” is written - [It is written] with two yods. Cast one [of them] into the middle of the word and read [it as]: “He shall not apply [lo yasikh],” which implies: Whoever is commanded not to apply [it] — neither to himself nor to others — [only] concerning him is another commanded not to apply [it] to him; and an idolater is not subject to the commandments.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:6:1.hebrew: כהן שסך בן בתו ישראל מתעגל בו כו' - ופי', כהן שסך את עצמו שמן, יכול בן בתו ישראל לבא להתעגל בו — ואפילו גדול, ושף עצמו באבי אמו — ואינו חושש. אלמא, כיון דבטלה בהתירא, בטלה. והכי תניא בהדיא בתוספתא דמסכת תרומות (פ"י ה"י): סך כהן את עצמו שמן של תרומה, ומביא בן בתו ישראל ומעגלו על גביו. ובן בתו ישראל דנקט — משום דרגיל אצלו, והוא הדין לאחריני:
Rashi on Keritot 7a:6:1.english: A priest who applied [oil], the son of his daughter [who is] an Israelite may rub against him, etc. - And the explanation is: [In the case of] a priest who applied oil to himself, the son of his daughter [who is] an Israelite may come to rub against him — and even an adult — and rub himself against his mother's father, and he need not be concerned. Evidently, once it was nullified in a permitted manner, it is nullified. And so it is taught explicitly in the Tosefta of Tractate Terumot (10:10): “A priest applies teruma oil to himself, and brings the son of his daughter [who is] an Israelite and rolls him upon his back.” And that it stated “the son of his daughter [who is] an Israelite” is because he is frequently with him, but the same law applies to others.

Rashi on Keritot 7a:8:1.hebrew: שאינו מביא אשם תלוי - שאין אשם תלוי בא אלא על ספק חטאת קבועה, כדמפרש בפ' בתרא (לקמן כריתות כה.):
Rashi on Keritot 7a:8:1.english: That he does not bring a provisional guilt offering - For a provisional guilt offering is brought only for uncertainty regarding a fixed sin offering, as is explained in the last chapter (below, Keritot 25a).
